headline: Railroad safety concerns near Emily Street discussed; fencing and warning signs remain under review.
summary: Councilor Zaida Govan and an Emily Street resident raised concerns about children and pedestrians near the tracks. Andy Koziol of MassDOT said CSX privately owns the rail corridor and MassDOT does not regulate or maintain it. Councilors Martin and Govan plan to talk with CSX and Amtrak, and a follow-up meeting with MassDOT and DPW was proposed for about two weeks later.

Public Portion 
 1. Discussion on Railroad Safety Concerns. 
On November 10, 2026, the Public Safety Committee, chaired by Councilor Gerry Martin, met to 
discuss railroad safety concerns near Emily Street in the Indian Orchard neighborhood following 
incidents involving pedestrians and animals along the railroad tracks. Councilor Zaida Govan 
raised concerns regarding the absence of protective fencing and warning signage near the 
residential area. An Emily Street resident described safety concerns involving children and 
neighborhood access to the tracks and requested consideration of additional signage and fencing 
to help prevent future incidents. The committee discussed potential safety improvements and the 
responsibilities of the agencies involved. 
 
Andy Koziol, Deputy Rail Administrator with the Massachusetts Department of Transportation 
(MassDOT), explained that the railroad corridor is privately owned by CSX, with rail operations 
involving CSX, Norfolk Southern, and Amtrak. He clarified that MassDOT does not directly 
regulate or maintain the privately owned corridor and that federal authorities oversee railroad 
operations. Discussion addressed possible safety measures, including fencing, warning signs, and 
community education initiatives. Council President Tracye Whitfield raised questions regarding 
potential funding through MassDOT's Complete Streets and other pedestrian safety grant 
programs. Koziol indicated that he would consult with MassDOT colleagues regarding 
applicable funding opportunities. Members also discussed property ownership considerations and 
whether permission from CSX would be required for improvements within the railroad corridor. 
 
The committee discussed coordinating with the City's Department of Public Works to explore 
available funding and potential safety improvements. Councilors Martin and Govan indicated 
their intention to continue discussions with CSX and Amtrak regarding possible cooperation on 
fencing and other preventive measures. A follow-up committee meeting was proposed within 
approximately two weeks, with MassDOT and DPW participation, to review available options 
and funding opportunities. Community education was also identified as a potential component of 
future safety efforts. No formal vote or recommendation to the full City Council was recorded, 
and the proposed safety measures remained under review. The meeting concluded at 5:24 p.m.
